evidence.description: Authors describe undergraduate experimental data, online survey-site access, CSV download, Excel processing and SPSS analysis.
evidence.quote:
Item 2. Generation of the Data
As described in the manuscript, data were collected from undergraduate business school students
via laboratory and online studies using z-Tree software and Qualtrics between April 19, 2017
and April 28, 2017 and between July 7, 2020 and July 17, 2020. Brian Gale and Jessen Hobson
have access to the raw data via the online survey site. The data were downloaded in csv files,
processed in Microsoft Excel, and statistically analyzed using SPSS. The experimental materials
for the primary experiment and supplemental experiment are provided as a separate file. The file
name is “Elliott Gale Hobson Research Materials” and is available to download as an online
appendix on JAR’s website.

evidence.description: Datasheet states primary-analysis code is included and that financial identifiers do not apply.

Item 5. Code Used to Conduct Primary Analyses
The code to conduct the primary analyses is available at the end of this document. As the data

evidence.description: Table 1 purpose and embedded SPSS SORT/SPLIT/MEANS/MIXED syntax, including native model settings.
evidence.quote:
Data Analyses

Table 1

We use a mixed linear model to test the effect of our independent variables (Push, Relevance,
and their interaction) on our dependent variable Est_Err_Perc. We also include Period as a
control variable. The following SPSS syntax generated results reported in Table 1.


Table 1, Panel A

SORT CASES BY Condition.
SPLIT FILE SEPARATE BY Condition.

MEANS TABLES=Est_Err_Perc BY Period
 /CELLS=MEAN STDDEV COUNT.


Table 1, Panels B and C

SPLIT FILE OFF.

MIXED Est_Err_Perc BY NoPush_1 Mixed_1 WITH Period
 /CRITERIA=DFMETHOD(SATTERTHWAITE) CIN(95) MXITER(100) MXSTEP(10)
SCORING(1)
  SINGULAR(0.000000000001) HCONVERGE(0, ABSOLUTE) LCONVERGE(0,
ABSOLUTE) PCONVERGE(0.000001, ABSOLUTE)
 /FIXED=NoPush_1 Mixed_1 NoPush_1*Mixed_1 Period | SSTYPE(3)
 /METHOD=REML
 /REPEATED=Period | SUBJECT(Part_#) COVTYPE(DIAG)
 /EMMEANS=TABLES(NoPush_1*Mixed_1) COMPARE(NoPush_1) ADJ(BONFERRONI)
 /EMMEANS=TABLES(NoPush_1*Mixed_1) COMPARE(Mixed_1) ADJ(BONFERRONI) .

evidence.description: Table 2 purpose and Panel A embedded SPSS mixed-model syntax.
evidence.quote:
Table 2

We use a mixed linear model to test the effects of Earnings, Forecast, Push, and the interaction
of Forecast and Push on our dependent variable Value_Estimate for the High Relevance
conditions (Panel A). We use a mixed linear model to test the effects of Earnings, Forecast,
Irrelevant, Push, the interaction of Forecast and Push, and the interaction of Irrelevant and Push
on our dependent variable Value_Estimate for the Mixed Relevance conditions (Panel B).
Finally, we use a mixed linear model to test the effects of Earnings, Forecast, Relevance, and the
interaction of Forecast and Relevance on our dependent variable Value_Estimate for the Push
conditions (Panel C). The following SPSS syntax generated results reported in Table 2.


Table 2, Panel A

SORT CASES BY Mixed_1 a1_1ifview.
SPLIT FILE SEPARATE BY Mixed_1 a1_1ifview.

MIXED Val_Estim BY NoPush_1 WITH C1_plus_c2_TOTAL Forecast_total
 /CRITERIA=DFMETHOD(SATTERTHWAITE) CIN(95) MXITER(100) MXSTEP(10)
SCORING(1)
  SINGULAR(0.000000000001) HCONVERGE(0, ABSOLUTE) LCONVERGE(0,
ABSOLUTE) PCONVERGE(0.000001, ABSOLUTE)

evidence.description: Table 4 supplemental experiment means, t-test and mixed-model syntax.
evidence.quote:
Table 4

We use an independent samples t-test to test the effect of Relevance on forecast acquisition for
our Push conditions in the supplemental experiment. We also use a mixed linear model to test
the effects of Earnings, Forecast, Relevance, and the interaction of Forecast and Relevance on
our dependent variable Value_Estimate for the Push conditions in the supplemental experiment.
The following SPSS syntax generated results reported in Table 4.


Table 4, Panels A and B

SORT CASES BY Condition.
SPLIT FILE SEPARATE BY Condition.

MEANS TABLES=Acq_AVERAGE
 /CELLS=MEAN COUNT STDDEV.

SPLIT FILE OFF.

T-TEST GROUPS=Condition(1 2)
 /MISSING=ANALYSIS
 /VARIABLES=Acq_AVERAGE
 /CRITERIA=CI(.95).


Table 4, Panel C

SORT CASES BY Acquire_Forecast.
SPLIT FILE SEPARATE BY Acquire_Forecast.

MIXED Value_Est BY Condition WITH C1C2_cum Forecast_total
 /CRITERIA=DFMETHOD(SATTERTHWAITE) CIN(95) MXITER(100) MXSTEP(10)
SCORING(1)
  SINGULAR(0.000000000001) HCONVERGE(0, ABSOLUTE) LCONVERGE(0,
ABSOLUTE) PCONVERGE(0.000001, ABSOLUTE)

 /METHOD=REML
